title: Cocomplete preaisles contain transfinite extensions of complexes
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal V$. Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category with $\mathcal V$-small Hom sets and all colimits indexed by $\mathcal V$-small categories [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian, def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $Q:\mathrm{CoCh}(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ be the unbounded derived localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal V_0$ be a strictly full subcategory of $D(\mathcal A)$ containing zero and closed under $\mathcal V$-small coproducts, $[1]$, and extensions: the middle object of a distinguished triangle belongs to $\mathcal V_0$ whenever both end objects do. Let $\theta$ be a $\mathcal V$-small ordinal and $(E_\beta^\bullet)_{\beta\leq\theta}$ an ordinal-indexed diagram of complexes, with $E_0^\bullet=0$, all transition maps degreewise monomorphisms, and $E_\lambda^\bullet=\varinjlim_{\beta<\lambda}E_\beta^\bullet$ degreewise at every nonzero limit $\lambda\leq\theta$. If $Q(E_{\beta+1}^\bullet/E_\beta^\bullet)\in\mathcal V_0$ for every $\beta<\theta$, then $Q(E_\theta^\bullet)\in\mathcal V_0$. No boundedness, compactness, or direct-summand closure hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Step 2, middle t-structure existence input. Agent-formulated auxiliary transfinite-closure lemma for the set-generated-aisle proof; this assertion is not proved in the blueprint. WANTED: a general reference proving that cocomplete preaisles in Grothendieck derived categories are closed under filtered homotopy colimits/transfinite extensions. No Stacks tag states this assertion.

mathlib_searches.query: If successive quotients of a continuous ordinal filtration of complexes lie in a coproduct and positive shift closed extension closed subcategory then the filtered complex lies in it
mathlib_searches.verdict: no match: filtered colimits and AB5 for complexes exist, but no result concerns a general cocomplete preaisle or its transfinite extensions.
no match: probability filtrations and simplicial anodyne extensions do not state the derived preaisle assertion.
